bug_report: A tenant is disputing their monthly SLA report: our report says 99.7% uptime for the period, but their ops team swears the service met 99.9% and their own monitoring agrees. downtime_minutes is producing a bigger number than the outage time the tenant actually experienced. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix downtime_minutes so the report matches real downtime, without breaking existing behaviour.

conversations.text: The uptime report double-counts a bad night: three alerts for what was one outage, plus a few one-ping blips that shouldn't count at all.
Two fixes then: merge overlapping or touching incident windows into one outage before summing, and drop anything under a minute — sub-60-second blips are monitoring noise, not downtime.
Right, and measure that minute on the merged window, not the raw alerts — three 30-second alerts back to back are one 90-second outage, not three ignorable blips.
Agreed. And maintenance windows we schedule stay excluded from downtime as they are today?
Yes, planned maintenance never counts against the SLA — subtract any overlap with a maintenance window.
Settled: merge overlapping/touching incident windows, ignore merged outages under 60 seconds, and subtract every maintenance overlap from what remains.

Amendment after the Q2 audit: legal flagged that ops has been declaring 'emergency maintenance' DURING incidents and the tool then writes the outage off. The auditors' rule is that maintenance only shields the SLA when customers had real notice.
So the maintenance exclusion needs a notice condition. Where's the line?
Twenty-four hours. A maintenance window only excludes downtime if its announced_at timestamp is at least 24 hours before the window starts. Short-notice maintenance counts as ordinary downtime.

Amending the rule, superseding the old subtract-all-maintenance behaviour: merging and the 60-second blip floor stay as decided; maintenance overlap is excluded ONLY when announced at least 24h before start — short-notice windows count against the SLA.
That's the rule the report has to implement going forward.

policy: merge overlapping incident windows; ignore merged blips <60s; exclude maintenance ONLY when announced >=24h before start (post-amendment)
non_guessable: the AMENDED maintenance rule (all-maintenance-excluded -> 24h-notice only); the chat-A rule passes the repro but fails hidden
